label: EU(7)-PIM: carbamazepine
title: Carbamazepine in an older person
statement: Carbamazepine | In lists: 5 (A); 5 (B) | Main reason: Increased risk of SIADH-like syndrome; adverse events like carbamazepine-induced confusion and agitation, atrioventricular block and bradycardia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Adjust dose to the response and serum concentration. E | Alternatives: Levetiracetam[d]; gabapentin[d]; lamotrigine[d]; valproic acid[d]. E

plain_summary: Carbamazepine can cause low blood sodium, confusion, agitation and a slow heart rhythm in older people.

medicine_groups.name: Carbamazepine
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, controlled-release tablets, chewable tablets and liquid all count.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a person aged 65 or older has at least one supply of carbamazepine (Group A). Any strength counts. If age is missing and carbamazepine is supplied, report only a possible finding and ask whether the person is 65 or older.
cannot_be_seen: Why carbamazepine was started (epilepsy, nerve pain or mood), blood levels of carbamazepine, sodium level, heart rhythm, and whether it is working.
ask_the_gp: Whether carbamazepine is still the right choice for this person and whether a sodium level and carbamazepine blood level are due.
